messages:
maya: Quick follow-up to the on-prem packaging RFC — I sketched a concrete proposal for image retirement + rollback semantics in air-gapped registries. TL;DR: introduce a tombstone + activation-marker approach, keep last-3 activated manifests, and enforce a 7-day grace window before garbage-collect. Looking for concerns on safety and operator UX.

len: Nice, shorter is good. My main worry is rollback speed if GC has removed layers. How does the proposal ensure a fast path to restore a prior image without re-ingesting large blobs? :thinking:

maya: Right — the idea is to never delete layers referenced by an "activated" manifest. Tombstone only applies to non-activated manifests. Pruning marks non-activated manifests with a prune-time; operator GC only deletes blobs when prune-time + grace_window has elapsed and no "pinned" policy exists.

alex: Two questions: signature/key rotation implications, and operator node failures during activation. If the signature on a retained manifest is old and KMS keys have rotated, can we still verify it? Also if an operator crashes mid-activate, do we end up with a half-activated state?

priya: For signatures we store the verifying public key(s) alongside the signed manifest (not the private key). Rotation: support keyset history in the local verifier config so we can validate older signatures for X days. We can add a short header in the manifest metadata: "valid-with-keys" that lists acceptable key IDs.

priya: On half-activations: make activation idempotent and two-phase: 1) write activation marker referencing manifest-id + epoch, 2) once all nodes ack the marker, flip the active pointer. If a node crashes, other nodes will complete. If activation never completes within timeout, operator can inspect and requeue.

sam: Operator UX — suggest a single command for emergency rollbacks that re-points the active pointer immediately and triggers a cluster-wide pull of the prior manifest. Example: `rdoctl package rollback --to sha256:abcd1234 --force` which does: write activation marker, bump epoch, instruct nodes to pull. Should also emit telemetry for success/failure.

maya: That CLI flow works. I want to avoid forcing massive re-pulls during normal operations. So we should prefer a mirror-first approach: before retiring a manifest, kick off a background mirror to a cold store that is reachable from restore nodes (maybe via removable media or a bastion). Only if mirror fails twice do we allow immediate GC after admin ack.

len: Mirror-first + grace window sounds safe. But how big should the grace window be? 7 days? 30 days? We need data from adoption patterns. Maybe make it configurable per-customer with a sane default of 7 days.

alex: Agree on configurable. One more: how do we handle manifests that differ only by tag/metadata but share blobs? GC should dedupe blobs globally, not per-manifest. Implementation note: keep a blob-refcount table in the local registry (persisted). GC decrements refcount when manifest removed.

priya: +1 for refcount. Also add a compacting job that periodically squashes tombstone metadata so the operator list view doesn't grow unbounded. That job can be paused during high-load windows.

ops-bot: build-bundle-174: :white_check_mark: bundle build OK (sha256:abcd1234) — automated mirror job scheduled to nodes at 2023-11-26T12:05:00Z

sam: Edge-case: air-gapped customer with strictly offline upgrade policy who refuses any automated mirror. For them the operator must expose a manual export flow to produce a signed export bundle (including blobs) that admins can physically transport. The import path should verify signatures and rehydrate refcounts.

maya: Good call. We'll add a `rdoctl package export --manifest sha256:... --signed` flow and a corresponding `rdoctl package import --signed-bundle /media/usb/bundle.tar` that validates and inserts without triggering GC for N days.

len: Operational playbook bullets: 1) plan retirement window (default 7d) 2) kick mirror job (automatic unless disabled) 3) put manifest into tombstone state 4) after grace window and successful mirror, GC cleans blobs 5) operator retains audit + ability to drain rollback marker within grace.

priya: UX: registry UI should show timeline: created -> activated -> tombstoned -> mirrored -> prunable with timestamps and quick actions: export / rollback / extend-grace.

alex: Security check: ensure that tombstone and activation markers are signed by operator keys and logged to audit (immutable log). That prevents tampering via compromised operator node.

maya: I'll update the RFC with these specifics (two-phase activation, keyset history, mirror-first, explicit export path, refcounting, grace window default 7d). I'll also add a sample operator CLI flow and the minimal JSON fields for manifest metadata. Example manifest metadata snippet:```json
{
  "id": "sha256:abcd1234",
  "created": "2025-02-10T18:22:00Z",
  "state": "activated",
  "valid_with_keys": ["key-id-2024-05"],
  "tombstone_at": null
}
```

sam: :thumbsup: sounds good. We should schedule a quick runbook dry-run with a couple of SREs next week.

maya: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC update in a follow-up thread and attach the CLI/CRD sketches. :eyes:
